questions.prompt: For an ideal gas, which is larger: \(C_P\) or \(C_V\)?
questions.answer:
For an ideal gas,
\[
C_P>C_V
\]
At constant pressure, heat input must both raise internal energy and supply expansion work.

questions.prompt: State Mayer's relation for an ideal gas.
questions.answer:
Mayer's relation for an ideal gas is
\[
C_P-C_V=R
\]

questions.prompt: Find the heat needed to raise \(2.0\,\mathrm{mol}\) of ideal gas by \(30\,\mathrm{K}\) at constant volume if \(C_V=20.8\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
At constant volume,
\[
Q_V=nC_V\Delta T
\]
\[
Q_V=(2.0)(20.8)(30)
\]
\[
Q_V=1.25\times10^3\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: For the same gas in the previous question, find the heat needed at constant pressure.
questions.answer:
First find
\[
C_P=C_V+R=20.8+8.31=29.1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}
\]
At constant pressure,
\[
Q_P=nC_P\Delta T
\]
\[
Q_P=(2.0)(29.1)(30)
\]
\[
Q_P=1.75\times10^3\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: For a monatomic ideal gas, derive \(C_P\) and \(\gamma\) from \(C_V=3R/2\).
questions.answer:
For a monatomic ideal gas,
\[
C_V=\frac{3}{2}R
\]
Using Mayer's relation,
\[
C_P=C_V+R=\frac{3}{2}R+R=\frac{5}{2}R
\]
Therefore
\[
\gamma=\frac{C_P}{C_V}=\frac{(5/2)R}{(3/2)R}=\frac{5}{3}
\]

questions.prompt: A gas has \(\gamma=1.40\). Derive \(C_V\) and \(C_P\) in terms of \(R\).
questions.answer:
Use
\[
\gamma=\frac{C_P}{C_V}
\]
and
\[
C_P-C_V=R
\]
Since \(C_P=\gamma C_V\),
\[
\gamma C_V-C_V=R
\]
\[
C_V=\frac{R}{\gamma-1}
\]
For \(\gamma=1.40\),
\[
C_V=\frac{R}{0.40}=2.5R
\]
and
\[
C_P=\gamma C_V=(1.40)(2.5R)=3.5R
\]

questions.prompt: Show from the first law why \(C_P-C_V=R\) for an ideal gas.
questions.answer:
At constant volume,
\[
W=0
\]
so
\[
Q_V=\Delta U=nC_V\Delta T
\]
At constant pressure,
\[
Q_P=\Delta U+W
\]
For an ideal gas,
\[
\Delta U=nC_V\Delta T
\]
and
\[
W=p\Delta V=nR\Delta T
\]
Thus
\[
Q_P=nC_V\Delta T+nR\Delta T=n(C_V+R)\Delta T
\]
But also
\[
Q_P=nC_P\Delta T
\]
so
\[
C_P-C_V=R
\]

questions.prompt: An ideal gas is heated through \(\Delta T\) at constant pressure. Derive the fraction of the heat input that becomes expansion work in terms of \(\gamma\).
questions.answer:
At constant pressure, the expansion work is
\[
W=p\Delta V=nR\Delta T
\]
The heat input is
\[
Q=nC_P\Delta T
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{W}{Q}=\frac{R}{C_P}
\]
Using \(R=C_P-C_V\),
\[
\frac{W}{Q}=\frac{C_P-C_V}{C_P}=1-\frac{1}{\gamma}
\]
so
\[
\frac{W}{Q}=\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}
\]
